newsitem.title: JAPAN: IHI to forgive Brazil firm's debt of 11 bln yen.
newsitem.headline: IHI to forgive Brazil firm's debt of 11 bln yen.

text.p: Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries Co Ltd (IHI) said on Friday it would forgive 11 billion yen of a total 15 billion yen in debt at the Brazilian shipbuilding venture Industrias Verolme Ishbras S.A. (IVI) as part of IVI's restructuring plan.
IHI is expected to post a parent company net profit of 15 billion yen in the year to March 1997, despite the write-off, an IHI spokesman said.
IHI posted a parent net profit of 13.16 billion yen in 1995/96. IHI has a 19 percent stake in IVI, with the rest owned by Brazilian investors, the spokesman said.

IHI said it would write off the debt in the 1996/97 business year and offset the writeoff with income from the sale of shares in a domestic subsidiary which listed on the stock market last autumn, and from the weak yen.
The spokesman said IHI would announce its 1996/97 business results on May 26.
IVI has been in the red because of recession in the Brazilian shipbuilding industry. IHI was asked by the state of Rio de Janeiro last autumn to help IVI's reconstruction.
IHI has yet to decide about the remaining debt of four billion yen and its stake in IVI, the spokesman said.
